Federal customs officers at Nuevo Laredo seized a short firearm and 45 cartridges hidden inside computer equipment, according to Mexico's National Customs Agency (ANAM), in a release reported on October 31, 2026. A canine unit trained to detect high-risk merchandise found the hidden weapon, the agency said.

The Nuevo Laredo seizure was one of three coordinated operations by ANAM, the National Guard, the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection and the Attorney General's Office, which together netted three firearms and 698 cartridges in Chihuahua and Tamaulipas, according to the release.

In the other two operations, officers found a semiautomatic short firearm inside a suitcase on a passenger bus from El Paso crossing at the Córdova–Las Américas international bridge in Ciudad Juárez, and a long firearm with 653 cartridges hidden under the driver's seat of a vehicle at the Anzaldúas customs section in Reynosa, the release says. The three people involved and the seized material were turned over to the public prosecutor's office to determine their legal status.

ANAM said the operations show how physical inspections, non-intrusive review technology and canine units combine to fight illegal arms trafficking.

Sources:

  • Corresponsales.mx, "ANAM decomisa armas y casi 700 cartuchos en Chihuahua y Tamaulipas," October 31, 2026 (reporting an ANAM release)

title: Nuevo Laredo customs seize gun hidden in computer equipment
